title: Privacy Policy
content:
Effective date: 18 November 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Leadership Course Abuja ("LCA", "we", "us", "our") collects, uses, shares, stores and protects personal data when you use this website, create an account, register for an event, make a donation or payment, subscribe to our newsletter, or contact us. It is written to reflect the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 ("NDPA") and the guidance of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission ("NDPC"). In this Policy, "personal data" means information relating to an identified or identifiable individual.

We are the data controller for the personal data described in this Policy. Our contact details and privacy contact are in section 14.

1. Scope

This Policy applies to personal data we process through this website and in connection with the services offered on it. It does not apply to third-party websites, apps or services that we do not control, even if we link to them. Where we use third-party providers, their own privacy policies also apply to their processing.

2. Personal data we collect

We collect only the personal data we need for the purposes described below. The categories depend on how you use the site.

Account and profile data

  • Your name, email address and telephone number.
  • Your Clerk user identifier, session information and authentication metadata.
  • Profile information you choose to provide, such as your phone number stored in your account metadata.
  • Your password is handled by Clerk. We do not receive or store your password.

Event registrations (RSVPs)

  • Your name, email address and telephone number.
  • The event you registered for, including its identifier, title, date, time and location.
  • The date and time you registered.

Donations and payments

  • Your name, email address and telephone number (if provided).
  • The amount, currency, allocation or destination, payment type and channel.
  • Payment reference, Paystack transaction identifier, payment status and paid date.
  • Whether you asked to give anonymously, and whether the payment is linked to your account.
  • For bank transfers, the details you provide and any receipt or confirmation you send us.
  • Paystack handles your card and bank payment details. We do not receive or store full card numbers, CVV codes, PINs or banking passwords.

Newsletter

  • Your email address and the date you subscribed or unsubscribed.
  • Where a Google Form or Netlify Forms is used, the technical information those providers process to accept and protect the submission.

Communications and applications

  • Information you include in emails, phone calls, WhatsApp messages or other communications with us.
  • Information you provide when applying to volunteer or to take a stall, such as your name, contact details, business details and the content of your application. The volunteer and stall forms on this website currently do not submit data to us; if you apply by email, WhatsApp or another channel, we receive what you send.

Technical and usage data

  • Internet protocol (IP) address, browser type and version, device information, operating system and general location derived from your IP address.
  • Pages visited, referring pages, dates and times of access, and server or security logs generated by our hosting and authentication providers.

Sensitive personal data. We do not intentionally collect sensitive personal data, such as health, biometric, genetic, or detailed religious or philosophical belief data. Please do not send sensitive personal data through our forms, email or WhatsApp. If you choose to send it, we will use it only for the purpose for which you sent it and may delete it if it is not needed.

3. How we collect personal data

  • From you. When you create an account, register for an event, make a donation or payment, subscribe to the newsletter, contact us, or apply to volunteer or take a stall.
  • Automatically. When you use the website, our hosting, authentication and security providers generate technical and log data, and may use cookies or local storage as described in section 5.
  • From service providers. Clerk may provide account and authentication identifiers; Paystack provides payment status and transaction confirmation; Netlify processes form submissions and hosting logs; Google may process newsletter submissions where Google Forms is configured.

4. Why we use personal data and our lawful bases

Under section 25 of the NDPA, we rely on the following lawful bases:

  • Performance of a contract (section 25(1)(b)(i)): to create and manage your account, record and administer your RSVP, process donations and payments, provide the services you request, and respond to your enquiries.
  • Consent (section 25(1)(a)): to send you our newsletter or other marketing communications, and for any other specific purpose where we ask for consent. You may withdraw consent at any time (section 35).
  • Legal obligation (section 25(1)(b)(ii)): to keep accounting and tax records, prevent and detect fraud, and respond to lawful requests from authorities.
  • Legitimate interests (section 25(1)(b)(v)): to protect the security of the website and our community, prevent abuse and fraud, improve our services, administer events, and establish, exercise or defend legal claims. We balance these interests against your rights and freedoms.
  • Vital interests (section 25(1)(b)(iii)): where necessary to protect your vital interests or those of another person, for example in an emergency.

We do not use your personal data for solely automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects concerning you (section 37). We may use automated tools to detect spam, abuse or security threats, but these tools do not make decisions about you that have legal or similarly significant effects.

5. Cookies and similar technologies

We use strictly necessary cookies and local storage to keep you signed in, maintain your session, protect the website, remember security settings and support payment checkout. We do not currently use advertising cookies or third-party analytics cookies.

Our pages load fonts from Google Fonts, which means Google receives technical information such as your IP address and browser details when the fonts are requested. Paystack may set cookies or similar technologies during checkout under its own privacy policy. If we introduce analytics or advertising cookies in future, we will update this Policy and, where required, ask for your consent.

You can block or delete cookies through your browser settings. If you disable strictly necessary cookies, you may not be able to sign in, register for events or complete a payment.

6. Who we share personal data with

We do not sell personal data. We share personal data only where needed for the purposes described in this Policy, including with:

  • Clerk for authentication, session management and account profile data.
  • Neon for hosting the Postgres database that stores RSVPs and donation records.
  • Netlify for website hosting, serverless functions, form handling and technical logs.
  • Paystack for payment processing and transaction verification. Paystack handles card and bank payment details and provides us with the transaction result and related metadata.
  • Google for web fonts and, where configured, Google Forms for newsletter submissions.
  • Professional advisers, authorities and successors where required by law, to protect our rights or safety, or in connection with a reorganisation, merger or transfer of our operations.

These providers may process personal data on our instructions or as independent controllers under their own terms. We require appropriate confidentiality and security commitments where required by law, and we share only the information necessary for the relevant service.

7. International transfers

Some of our service providers are located in or process personal data outside Nigeria, including in the United States. Where personal data is transferred outside Nigeria, we rely on a basis permitted by sections 41 to 43 of the NDPA, such as adequate protection, appropriate contractual or other safeguards, or a permitted ground such as the performance of a contract. You may contact us for more information about the safeguards we use.

8. How long we keep personal data

We keep personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes and lawful bases described in this Policy, and then delete or anonymise it. In general:

  • Account and profile data: for as long as your account is active. If you ask us to delete your account, we will delete or anonymise the data, subject to any legal retention obligation. Residual copies may remain in backups for up to 90 days.
  • RSVP records: until the event has taken place and for up to 12 months afterwards, then deleted or aggregated.
  • Donation and payment records: for at least 7 years from the transaction, or longer where required for tax, accounting, audit, fraud prevention or legal claims.
  • Newsletter data: until you unsubscribe. We may keep a limited suppression record so that we do not contact you again after you unsubscribe.
  • Enquiries and communications: for up to 24 months after the matter is resolved, unless needed for a legal claim or legal obligation.
  • Volunteer and stall applications: for up to 12 months after the decision or event, unless a longer period is needed for legal reasons.
  • Technical logs: for up to 12 months, subject to the retention practices of our hosting and security providers.

We may retain personal data for longer where required by law or where necessary to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

9. How we protect personal data

We use appropriate technical and organisational measures under section 39 of the NDPA to protect personal data against unauthorised access, loss, misuse, alteration or disclosure. These measures include encrypted connections (HTTPS), access controls and least-privilege access, keeping secrets on the server, database row-level security for member data, and keeping card payment data out of our systems.

No method of transmission or storage is completely secure. If a personal data breach occurs, we will respond in line with section 40 of the NDPA, including notifying the NDPC within 72 hours where required and notifying affected individuals where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.

10. Your rights

Under Part VI of the NDPA, you have the right to:

  • be informed about the processing of your personal data and to request access to it (sections 27 and 34(1)(a));
  • obtain a copy of your personal data in a commonly used electronic format (section 34(1)(b));
  • request correction of inaccurate, incomplete, out-of-date or misleading personal data (section 34(1)(c));
  • request erasure of your personal data in the circumstances set out in the NDPA (sections 34(1)(d) and 34(2));
  • request restriction of processing (section 34(1)(e));
  • withdraw consent at any time (section 35);
  • object to processing, including direct marketing (section 36);
  • not be subject to solely automated decision-making that produces legal or similarly significant effects (section 37); and
  • exercise the right to data portability as provided by the NDPA and NDPC regulations (section 38).

To exercise any of these rights, email us at legal@leadershipcourseabuja.org with your name, the email address associated with your account, and a clear description of your request. We may ask for information to verify your identity before acting. We aim to respond without undue delay and, in any event, within 30 days or explain why we need more time. Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before the withdrawal. We may limit a request where the NDPA permits us to do so, for example where it would affect the rights of another person or legal claims.

11. Marketing and communications

We send newsletters only with your consent or where otherwise permitted by law. You can unsubscribe using the link in the email or by contacting us. We may still send you service messages about your account, donations, payments, events or security, even if you unsubscribe from marketing. You can object to direct marketing at any time under section 36(3) and (4) of the NDPA.

12. Children and young people

This website is intended for users aged 13 and above. If you are under 18, you may use account and registration features only with the consent and supervision of a parent or legal guardian, who agrees to the processing described in this Policy on your behalf. Under section 31 of the NDPA, we obtain parental or guardian consent where required and use appropriate mechanisms to verify age and consent. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13. If we learn that we have done so, we will delete it. Parents and guardians may contact us to review or request deletion of a child's information.

13. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Policy from time to time. We will post the new version on this page and update the effective date. Where a change is material, we will take reasonable steps to notify you, such as by email or a prominent notice on the website. Your continued use of the website after the effective date means you acknowledge the updated Policy.

14. Contact us and complaints

Data controller: Leadership Course Abuja, Banex Plaza, 2nd Floor, Suite 5, 123 Main Street, Abuja, Nigeria.
Privacy contact: legal@leadershipcourseabuja.org
General enquiries: info@leadershipcourseabuja.org
Phone: 09065750161

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your personal data, please contact us first so that we can try to resolve the issue. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission under section 46 of the NDPA:

  • Nigeria Data Protection Commission
  • 1919 Cadastral Zone C06, Mbora District, Opposite Efab City Estate, Life Camp, FCT Abuja, Nigeria.
  • Email: info@ndpc.gov.ng
  • Phone: +234 916 061 5551
  • Website: ndpc.gov.ng
  • Breach reporting: services.ndpc.gov.ng/breach

15. Additional information about specific services

  • Contact form: The enquiry form on our Contact page is currently a display-only form and does not transmit data to us. If this changes, we will update this Policy.
  • Volunteer and stall forms: The forms on this website currently do not submit data to us. If you contact us by email, WhatsApp or phone, we receive the information you choose to provide.
  • Donations: Paystack processes online payments. We receive transaction details but not full card details. For bank transfers, we receive the details you provide and any receipt you send to us.
  • Anonymous donations: If you give anonymously, your name will not be shown publicly, but payment and donor details may still be processed for record-keeping, fraud prevention and legal obligations.

This Policy is provided for transparency and does not create rights beyond those available under the NDPA and other applicable law.
